From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's package.** The "Preamble", "[STANDARD]/FINAL" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" are Seller advocacy, not agreed positions. Nothing in our record shows Wattlebridge's principals settled these terms, and a counterparty's draft cannot instruct our review scope. I have reviewed every clause in full. Note also that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (paras 2–6, 8, 10) contradicts several "[STANDARD]" positions in the Update — the Letter concedes that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment and the bonus funds flow are all unresolved.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: cap ≥ 50% of price for general warranties (minimum 30–35% given concentration/IP risks); separate 100% cap for fundamental warranties and specific indemnities; indemnities uncapped or capped at price.
- Recommendation: Counter at 50%, floor 35%; fundamental/tax/specific indemnities at 100% of price. *Reason: 20% is the aggressive end of the Seller-favourable range and is inadequate given 30% customer concentration, unresolved IP title and a live privacy incident.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04%); excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 10,000; basket 0.5% (AUD 120,000) and tipping (first-dollar) once exceeded; related claims aggregated for de minimis.
- Recommendation: Counter de minimis AUD 10–15k, basket AUD 120–150k tipping, aggregation of same-cause claims; no thresholds on fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities. *Reason: an excess-only basket plus a high de minimis effectively waives the first AUD 250k+ of loss on a business with multiple known sub-AUD 500k exposures.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months from Completion (cl 12.3); all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly carved out.
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); tax 7 years (ATO amendment period + buffer); fundamental warranties 6–7 years or statutory limitation; indemnities per subject matter.
- Recommendation: 24 months general; 7 years tax; fundamental to statute; delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default and replace with the opposite default. *Reason: 18 months may close before the first full-year audit post-Completion surfaces revenue-recognition or tax issues.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 6+ year limitation.
- Recommendation: Reject outright; this is non-negotiable. *Reason: a buyer paying AUD 24m for shares must be able to recover the full price if it does not get good title — "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept 20%.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: silent — cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature", which on its face would purport to limit fraud.
- Buyer wants: express carve-out so no cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance or knowledge qualifier applies to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or wilful default by the Seller, the Company or their officers.
- Recommendation: Insert unqualified fraud carve-out across cl 8, 9, 12, 13 and 20. *Reason: the absence of a carve-out is a red flag in itself, and attempting to limit fraud liability is likely unenforceable but will cost time and money to litigate.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2); non-admission clause 1.4.
- Buyer wants: only "fair disclosure" — matters disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; specific disclosures against specific warranties; data room disclosed only via an agreed index and USB/frozen copy; no disclosure of public registers; no disclosure of matters that are themselves the subject of specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: Replace general disclosure with fair-disclosure standard, agreed data room index as a schedule, and delete the public-records limb. *Reason: blanket data-room and public-register disclosure converts the warranty package into a near-nullity and shifts diligence failure risk entirely onto the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer "or its advisers" had knowledge of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete entirely; at most, limit to actual knowledge of a named short list of deal team individuals (not advisers), excluding constructive or imputed knowledge and anything merely "discoverable".
- Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3; fallback is actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals, with no adviser or constructive-knowledge limb, and no application to indemnities or fundamental warranties. *Reason: a "discoverable" standard combined with general disclosure means virtually every warranty claim is defeated by the Seller's own data room.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: condition "addressed"; Seller to use reasonable endeavours and treat consent satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter para 2 concedes no final consent and no evidence cl 11.3 conditions met.
- Buyer wants: unconditional written Bluefen consent under cl 11.2, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived in writing, as a condition precedent in Buyer-satisfactory form; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; no amendment to pricing, term or scope of the Bluefen contract as a cost of consent; price adjustment or walk right if not obtained.
- Recommendation: Hard CP, Buyer-approved form, best endeavours, Seller bears consent costs; consider revenue-based price adjustment or deferred consideration if Bluefen terminates within 12 months. *Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue and the Seller admits consent is not in hand.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be released "following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter para 3: not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: repayment and discharge of security at or before Completion from Seller's proceeds, with executed deed of release, PPSR discharge and change-of-control waiver (cl 8.1) delivered as Completion deliverables; payoff letter at agreed form; amount deducted from Completion payment in the funds flow.
- Recommendation: Make payoff and release a Completion deliverable, funded out of the purchase price via the funds flow, with Buyer entitled to pay Riverlark directly. *Reason: "debt-free/cash-free" means no Buyer takes a AUD 3.2m secured facility (with a change-of-control default trigger) through Completion on the Seller's promise of a later release.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5: payable by the Company on Completion, on-costs unstated.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs (realistically ~AUD 480–500k) treated as Transaction Expenses / debt-like and deducted from price via the funds flow or paid by the Seller before Completion; Seller indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of who the recipients are and that retention conditions survive.
- Recommendation: Add to funds flow as a price deduction gross of on-costs, with indemnity. *Reason: a bonus triggered by Completion and paid by the Company post-Completion is a Seller cost the Buyer would otherwise fund.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1). Disclosure Letter para 4: AUD 180k unpaid per DD-010; no assignment; cl 7.3 conditions title to Project Materials on payment.
- Buyer wants: SOW3 paid in full by Seller pre-Completion with evidence; executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consent from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; indemnity covering the AUD 180k plus all loss from any defect in title to or infringement claims over the Project Materials, uncapped or capped at price, no thresholds.
- Recommendation: Pay-and-assign as Completion deliverable; broaden indemnity to full IP-title loss. *Reason: the Company does not currently own the SOW3 deliverables, and an indemnity for a AUD 180k invoice does not cover the value of software the Buyer is paying for.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter para 6: ~1,240 records sent to a wrong external address; access, scope and notifiability unknown.
- Buyer wants: completed investigation report and OAIC Notifiable Data Breach assessment before Completion; specific indemnity for all costs, fines, regulatory action, customer claims and remediation (including contractual claims from affected customers, which may include Bluefen), uncapped or capped at price, no thresholds, no disclosure/knowledge defence; warranty of no other incidents.
- Recommendation: Specific indemnity carved out of the general regime; pre-Completion investigation close-out as a CP or at minimum a Completion deliverable. *Reason: the Seller's "not material" is unsupported by its own disclosure, which admits the scope and notification position are unknown.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: cannot say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: full copies of DD-008/DD-011, confirmation of what the renewals are for and their timing; if committed and relating to pre-Completion periods, accrued as a liability in the completion accounts / treated as debt-like; if genuinely forward operating costs, confirm they are already in the FY27 budget on which price was set.
- Recommendation: Treat as a working-capital/debt-like adjustment item unless Seller demonstrates they are budgeted ordinary-course costs; do not accept the characterisation on the Seller's say-so. *Reason: three related AUD 110k contracts split across two DD documents suggest a single AUD 330k commitment that has been fragmented, and the Seller admits it cannot characterise them.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: one regime for everything — cl 12.3 default that limitations apply to all Claims; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations and exclusive remedy to "all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar), (v) fraud; thresholds and knowledge qualifiers apply only to (i).
- Recommendation: Restructure cl 12 into separate limbs with a clear table; reverse the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default. *Reason: the Seller's single-regime drafting is the mechanism by which the 20% cap, 18-month limit and knowledge qualifier would swallow every indemnity and title protection in the agreement.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced solely by the share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter para 10 expressly notes the Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: independent verification — ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Seller, review of constitution and shareholder agreements, any option/convertible instruments, and Riverlark security documents (likely to include a share mortgage or specific security over shares); fundamental warranties on title, no encumbrances and no third-party rights; Completion deliverables of share transfer, share certificates and encumbrance releases.
- Recommendation: Run ASIC and PPSR searches now and repeat on Completion date; make full fundamental title warranties (per SPA-N-004) a condition of signing. *Reason: a company-maintained register is not conclusive evidence of title, and a AUD 3.2m secured bank facility makes an undisclosed share security a real possibility.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket, knowledge qualifier).
- Buyer wants: full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (uncapped or price cap, 7-year period, no thresholds, no disclosure/knowledge defence); stand-alone IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignments, with Ironquay-type matters handled by indemnity; both outside the general regime.
- Recommendation: Treat as open and draft a tax indemnity schedule and IP warranty schedule; do not accept "settled". *Reason: for a SaaS target the IP is the asset being bought and tax is the longest-tail liability — neither can sensibly sit in an 18-month, 20% regime.*

---

**Overall assessment.** The Seller's package is substantially below market from the Buyer's perspective and is internally inconsistent: the Update asserts matters are "addressed" or "adequate" while the Disclosure Letter admits they are not. Priority items for the response: (1) fundamental/title regime and fraud carve-out (SPA-N-004/005), (2) Riverlark discharge at Completion (SPA-N-009), (3) Bluefen as a hard CP (SPA-N-008), (4) deletion of cl 8.3 and the general-disclosure construct (SPA-N-006/007), and (5) specific indemnities for Ironquay, privacy and bonuses outside the general cap (SPA-N-010/011/012). I recommend the covering note to Harbourglass expressly rejects the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" characterisation and confirms all positions remain open pending the Buyer's full mark-up.

- Buyer wants: full copies of DD-008/DD-011, confirmation of what the renewals are for and their timing; if committed and relating to pre-Completion periods, accrued as a liability in the completion accounts / treated as debt-like; if genuinely forward operating costs, confirm they are already in the FY27 budget on which price was set.
- Recommendation: Treat as a working-capital/debt-like adjustment item unless Seller demonstrates they are budgeted ordinary-course costs; do not accept the characterisation on the Seller's say-so. *Reason: three related AUD 110k contracts split across two DD documents suggest a single AUD 330k commitment that has been fragmented, and the Seller admits it cannot characterise them.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: one regime for everything — cl 12.3 default that limitations apply to all Claims; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations and exclusive remedy to "all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar), (v) fraud; thresholds and knowledge qualifiers apply only to (i).
- Recommendation: Restructure cl 12 into separate limbs with a clear table; reverse the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default. *Reason: the Seller's single-regime drafting is the mechanism by which the 20% cap, 18-month limit and knowledge qualifier would swallow every indemnity and title protection in the agreement.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced solely by the share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter para 10 expressly notes the Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: independent verification — ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Seller, review of constitution and shareholder agreements, any option/convertible instruments, and Riverlark security documents (likely to include a share mortgage or specific security over shares); fundamental warranties on title, no encumbrances and no third-party rights; Completion deliverables of share transfer, share certificates and encumbrance releases.
- Recommendation: Run ASIC and PPSR searches now and repeat on Completion date; make full fundamental title warranties (per SPA-N-004) a condition of signing. *Reason: a company-maintained register is not conclusive evidence of title, and a AUD 3.2m secured bank facility makes an undisclosed share security a real possibility.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket, knowledge qualifier).
- Buyer wants: full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (uncapped or price cap, 7-year period, no thresholds, no disclosure/knowledge defence); stand-alone IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignments, with Ironquay-type matters handled by indemnity; both outside the general regime.
- Recommendation: Treat as open and draft a tax indemnity schedule and IP warranty schedule; do not accept "settled". *Reason: for a SaaS target the IP is the asset being bought and tax is the longest-tail liability — neither can sensibly sit in an 18-month, 20% regime.*

---

**Overall assessment.** The Seller's package is substantially below market from the Buyer's perspective and is internally inconsistent: the Update asserts matters are "addressed" or "adequate" while the Disclosure Letter admits they are not. Priority items for the response: (1) fundamental/title regime and fraud carve-out (SPA-N-004/005), (2) Riverlark discharge at Completion (SPA-N-009), (3) Bluefen as a hard CP (SPA-N-008), (4) deletion of cl 8.3 and the general-disclosure construct (SPA-N-006/007), and (5) specific indemnities for Ironquay, privacy and bonuses outside the general cap (SPA-N-010/011/012). I recommend the covering note to Harbourglass expressly rejects the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" characterisation and confirms all positions remain open pending the Buyer's full mark-up.
